title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-04
source: Audience Recording by Gerry Olsen. Sony TC-124 single-capstan portable cassette deck equipped with Sony F-99S One Point Stereo Dynamic Microphone IMP LOW (hand-held). 120 minute BASF normal bias tape. Lineage via Dan McDonald (droncit@yahoo.com): Master Audience Cassette->Nakamichi BX-1 (modified for flat transfer)-> Tascam DR-07MK2 (24-bit, 96kHz); DC8Forensics was used to apply the NAB curve for normal bias cassettes. Converted to 16-bit, 44.1kHz using 32-bit interpolation and a triangular high pass dither. After the NAB curve in a multifilter I applied a virtual vale and overtone generator for lost harmonics and used a channel blender to blend below 150 Hz to mono to minimize mic handling noise.

ai_review.summary: Clear, well‑EQ’d audience tape of the legendary June 4 1970 Fillmore West three‑part show, highlighted by a smoking St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording captures an exceptional three‑set night – acoustic, NRPS and electric – with vivid ambience that many reviewers say sounds “clear upfront” and benefits from a modest EQ boost.  The performance shines on the St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour medley and the China > Rider transition, while Jerry’s pedal‑steel work and Mickey’s “non‑country country” drumming are frequently praised.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently enthusiastic reviews highlight a strong musical performance (standout sequences, smooth set flow) and an audience tape that is clear and listenable despite being non‑soundboard.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners describe the tape as surprisingly clear with a lovely upfront sound; flat transfer benefits from boosted lows/highs and reduced mids.  First‑set portions are sourced from a soundboard, while the NRPS and electric sets are pure audience (matrix) recordings that ‘sizzle’ for many.

standout_songs: St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑part structure (acoustic → New Riders → electric) is praised for its natural progression and seamless transitions, especially the St. Stephen medley and China > Rider segue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel highlighted during NRPS set; noted for smooth transition from acoustic to electric guitar work.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey's drumming described as ‘decidedly non‑country country drums’, adding a distinctive feel.
